key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni-20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% relative to bare SA516 steel, giving the best protection among the tested coatings.
engineering_relevance: These coatings could improve oxidation protection for SA516 boiler steel exposed to high temperatures.
method: Apply Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN using HVOF and plasma spraying.
Characterize phases and microstructure using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: Bare steel showed intense oxide spalling and cracking, while improved coating performance was attributed to protective oxides, reduced porosity, and increased microhardness.
watch_item: Results cover 50 laboratory air-oxidation cycles; long-term durability in actual boiler environments remains unverified.
paper_title: Microstructure and high-temperature oxidation behaviour of HVOF and plasma sprayed Ni–Cr-based ceramic coatings on SA516 boiler steel
